questions.stem: LM picture of skeletal muscle (A).  By L.M. Each skeletal muscle fiber is a long cell with the following:  Sarcolemma: thick due to its fusion with the surrounding basal lamina & endomysium.  Nuclei: multiple oval peripheral nuclei. Their number corresponds to the number of fused mononucleated myoblasts.  Sarcoplasm: deeply acidophilic (mitochondria, sER, myofibrils) with uniformly placed transverse striations that appear clearly in longitudinal section. Dr. Ahmed Zahra 8 Histology WRITTEN

Sarcomere (EM picture of myofibrils) (A). Myofibrils (Sarcomere) • The portion of a myofibril between two adjacent Z lines is called sarcomere, it is the basic contractile unit of striated muscle, and so considered the functional unit in contraction. • Each myofibril shows alternating dark A bands & light I-bands, that explain the appearance of transverse striations and give the descriptive term striated muscle N.B. I bands are very short in contracted muscle & longer in relaxed muscle, the length of A bands remain constant. The higher magnification of the electron microscope : The myofibrils are composed of thick myosin and thin actin filaments: • The thick myosin filaments are restricted to the A- band. • I-band appears light (formed of only actin) & bisected by Z-line • A-band appear dark (formed of both myosin & actin) & bisected by H-zone • H-band appears paler (formed of myosin filaments only) & bisected by M-line. • M-line is produced by interconnections of adjacent myosin filaments. • Z-line is dense by condensed actin filaments, matrix material & other proteins (accessory proteins maintaining precise alignment of thin and thick filaments) as:
Titin, anchors thick myosin filaments to the Z-lines preventing excessive stretching of sarcomere

Dystrophin, a large protein, link the external lamina of the muscle cell, to actin filaments. Absence of this protein is associated with progressive muscular weakness (muscular dystrophy). Dr. Ahmed Zahra 9 Histology WRITTEN

Triad tubular system (A+). The Transverse tubules: • invaginations of sarcolemma, forming transverse tubules or T-tubules in the sarcoplasm to encircle all myofibrils. • located at the A-I band junctions and their lumens are continuous with the extracellular space. • Each T-tubule lies in-between a pair of wide terminal cisternae of the sarcoplasmic reticulum forming a triple structure called the triad tubular system. Function of skeletal muscles & the role of triad tubular system: Skeletal muscle → voluntary contraction (controlled by the will), except pharynx, esophagus & cremasteric muscles are involuntary. Steps of contraction:  The arrival of a nerve impulse to the neuromuscular junction triggers the depolarization of the sarcolemma of muscle fiber.  Depolarization is spread along the membranes of T-tubules into the depth of the muscle fiber.  It stimulates the sarcoplasmic reticulum to release the Ca+2 into the sarcoplasm  Ca+2 facilitates the complex sliding of the actin filaments over the myosin deeper toward the middle of A-band. During contraction: # shortening of sarcomere. # shortening of I-band. ‫مهم‬ # narrowing of H-zone or even disappear. # A-band do not change. # The length of actin & myosin filaments is not changed.  When depolarization stops: Ca+2 is actively pumped into the sarcoplasmic reticulum ,decreasing Ca+2 in the sarcoplasm & contraction stops (muscle relaxation). 4 Sarcoplasm contains: Dr. Ahmed Zahra 10 Histology WRITTEN

Clinically Important Points The anastomosis between the right and left coronary arteries is poor, especially in young age. Although it increases as age advances, it remains inadequate to provide an efficient collateral circulation if a large artery is suddenly blocked (the anastomosis opens slowly). A reduction in blood supply to the heart by a narrowing of a large branch leads to ischaemia of the heart muscle. This may cause angina pectoris manifested by an agonizing pain in the front of the chest behind the sternum which radiates (as referred pain) to the left shoulder and medial side of the arm. Blockage of a coronary artery or one of its main branches as in coronary thrombosis leads to myocardial infarction (death of part of myocardium). The right coronary artery supplies most of the conducting system of the heart. Blockage of its branches may cause arrhythmias (irregularities in heart beat). Pulmonary Trunk An arterial trunk which conveys deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs. It is 5 cm long. It lies behind the sternal end of the 2nd left intercostal space. The cartilages and muscles originate from mesenchyme of the 4th and 6th arches. Because of rapid proliferation of this mesenchyme, the laryngeal orifice changes in appearance from a sagittal slit to a T-shaped opening. Subsequently, when mesenchyme of the two arches transforms into the thyroid, cricoid, and arytenoid cartilages, the characteristic adult shape of the laryngeal orifice can be recognized. The laryngeal epithelium proliferates rapidly, resulting in a temporary occlusion of the lumen. Subsequently, vacuolization and recanalization produce a pair of lateral recesses (laryngeal ventricles). Bronchial tree During its separation from the foregut, the laryngo-tracheal tube forms the trachea and two bronchial buds.
